Theme 011 · Typography & graphic systems

Split-Flap Board

The whole film is a station departures board: every metric is a row of mechanical flaps that clatter through the alphabet and settle. Healthy rows land "ON TIME"; one row refuses to settle, flips to coral and holds, and the board waits for a human to call it.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Flap cell — a character tile with a split top/bottom half and a dark hinge; the only letterform in the film.
  • Board row — a metric name, its value and a status column, the way a timetable lists departures.
  • Status flaps — "ON TIME" in green, "HELD" in coral; the vocabulary of every health state.
  • Hero row — the anomaly promoted to 104 px flaps in coral, with a soft coral glow bleeding behind it.
  • Ghost row — half-flipped blank tiles above and below the action, for depth and constant low motion.
  • Action flaps — "ROLL BACK" and "START FREE" built from the same tiles inside a lit button frame.

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Cascade flip — top half rotateX 0→−90° (60 ms, power2.in), bottom half 90→0° (60 ms, power2.out), 4–10 interim glyphs per cell; a full settle ≈ 1 beat at 120 BPM.
  • Row wave — 30 ms stagger per cell, 120 ms between rows, so a 3-row block lands in exactly one bar.
  • Settle wobble — each final flap overshoots 4° (back.out(3), 120 ms); the anomaly row wobbles twice and locks on the downbeat.

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

Everyone can read a departures board instantly, and "the one row that stops" is a dramatic but calm way to show an anomaly. The motion is rhythmic by nature, so it cuts to music without any help. Risk: it has to feel mechanical even with the sound off, so flip timing matters more than detail.

Adapt to your product: list your own objects (deploys, invoices, jobs, tickets) as rows and map your states to status words. Keep rows to 9–10 characters and let a single row turn to your alert color.
